transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's, um, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

I, well, I hope I'm not overreacting or wasting your time, but... I've just been having this sort of constant restless feeling? It's probably just normal stress—I'm a retail buyer, so it gets a bit hectic—but I just feel like I'm wound a little too tight lately. I just can't seem to fully settle. And it's slightly embarrassing because it happens even when I'm really supposed to be calmly sitting, like during a long planning meeting at work. Or even when I'm just at home trying to relax with painting or, you know, doing yoga. I just can't seem to completely unwind. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Beyond feeling restless or wound up, have you noticed a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in the activities you usually enjoy?

Oh, um, no, not at all. I don't think so, anyway. I still really enjoy the things I usually do. Like the painting I mentioned—I still absolutely love it, and I'm still very interested in my work, too. 

It's really just the... the physical feeling of not being able to settle down while I'm doing those things, if that makes sense? But the actual joy and interest are definitely still there. I hope that's a good sign? I really try to stay positive and engaged. Does that answer your question okay?
About how long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I suppose I've always been a little high-energy, which I always thought was a good thing, you know? But this feeling of being so... wound up... I'd say it's been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. 

It kind of lined up with when my husband and I started having some conflicts with our in-laws. It just started taking over so much of our evenings, and I think that's when I really felt like I couldn't just sit and relax anymore. I know family stress is totally normal, and I really shouldn't let it get to me this much, but that's about when it started feeling a bit overwhelming. Does that sound like a normal reaction to stress, or am I overthinking it?
Do you often notice that your muscles feel tense, tight, or sore, such as in your shoulders, neck, or jaw?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I carry a little bit of tension in my shoulders sometimes, but I think everyone does, right? Especially sitting at a desk or dealing with, you know, just normal daily things. But it's nothing major, definitely not sore or painful or anything like that. I really try to keep good posture and stretch when I can. Is it okay if I don't have that symptom? I hope I'm not missing something I should be noticing.
Have you been having any difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep?

Oh, um, no, actually. My sleep is pretty good, thankfully. I mean, sometimes it takes me just a little bit to wind down at night, just because I'm still feeling a bit... energetic, I guess? But once I actually close my eyes, I fall asleep fine and I usually sleep right through the night. 

I feel really lucky about that, honestly, because I know how important rest is. Is it okay that my sleep is normal even though I feel so wound up during the day? I hope that doesn't make things more confusing for you to figure out.
When you feel this way, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of different topics or events in your life?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I worry excessively. I mean, I care about things, of course, like anyone does—making sure work is going well, hoping my family is okay. But it's not this constant, overwhelming worry about everything. 

It's more just... this physical feeling of needing to be doing something, rather than my mind spinning with all these anxious thoughts about different things going wrong. I try really hard to stay positive and not let things get to me. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find that your moods or how you feel about the people close to you can shift very suddenly or intensely?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my moods are pretty stable, I think. I love my family and friends, and that doesn't really change or swing back and forth. 

Sometimes I might get a little impatient if I'm feeling really restless and someone is moving slowly, but I don't get intensely angry or suddenly hate them or anything like that. I try really hard to be a supportive person to the people I care about. Is that what you mean? I just want to be sure I'm answering correctly so I'm not wasting your time.
Are you currently using any substances, such as caffeine, prescription medications, or anything else that might act as a stimulant?

Oh, no, I don't take anything like that. No prescription medications or, um, anything illegal, of course! I do have a cup of coffee in the mornings before work—just one, usually!—but that's really it. 

I try to be very careful about my health and what I put in my body. Is it okay that I drink a little coffee? I can definitely cut it out if you think it's making me too energetic or if it's bad for me. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to help you figure this out.
Have you ever found yourself in situations where you felt the need to break rules or deceive others to get what you wanted, even if it meant potentially hurting someone else's feelings?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I would never do that. I try really hard to be an honest person, and I would feel just awful if I ever hurt someone's feelings or, you know, deceived them on purpose. 

I mean, I'm a buyer for a retail company, so I negotiate a lot, but it's always above board and fair. I really pride myself on being someone people can trust. I hope you don't think I'm the kind of person who would break rules like that? I always try to do the right thing and be considerate of others.
When you are feeling this restless, do you ever find that your mind goes blank or that you have trouble concentrating on what you are doing?

Um, no, I don't think so. My mind doesn't really go blank. I actually feel like I can focus pretty well, even when I'm feeling a little... antsy. 

Like, my body might just want to be moving or doing something, but my brain is still completely on track. In my job, you know, keeping track of all the inventory and vendor contracts, I really have to stay sharp, and I always make sure I get my work done! I never let things slip through the cracks. 

I hope that's okay to say? I just don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job at work or that I can't handle my responsibilities. Am I explaining that right for you?
Looking back at your childhood, did you often find it difficult to sit still in class or feel like you were driven by a motor even when you were much younger?

Well, um... I suppose I was a bit energetic as a little girl. I mean, I think a lot of children are, right? It's perfectly normal for kids to have a lot of energy. 

But, um... I do remember in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes send notes home to my parents. It wasn't anything terrible! I just... I had a habit of popping out of my seat a little too often, or maybe talking over my classmates sometimes when I got excited. And I'd always rush to answer questions before the teacher even finished asking them. I just wanted to participate and show I knew the answer! 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker. I really always wanted to be a good student and please my teachers. Does that make sense? I mean, a lot of kids are just eager to learn like that, don't you think?
